newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Egypt says all but U.S. support Boutros-Ghali.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says all but U.S. support Boutros-Ghali.

text.p: The United States is expected to be isolated in the first Security Council poll on Boutros Boutros-Ghali's candidacy for a second term as U.N. secretary-general with the other 14 members voting in favour, a senior Egyptian diplomat said on Monday.

"There will be 14 votes on record in favour. They (the members) told me," Ambassador Nabil Elaraby told Reuters. Egypt, Botswana and Guinea-Bissau have prepared a resolution supporting Boutros-Ghali's candidacy.
A vote was not expected before late afternoon Monday, diplomats said.

Earlier in the day, the Security Council began its first day of consultations to nominate a secretary-general, with U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright under instructions to block a second term for Boutros-Ghali.
The current term of Boutros-Ghali, an Egyptian, expires on Dec. 31.

If a veto is cast, council members would again consult and give preference to other African candidates on the grounds that if a secretary-general was denied a second term, contrary to U.N. practice, he should be succeeded by someone from the same region.
